title: Forgiveness with Furqan Mohamed
body: We close this year’s Summer Series by reading poems that turn forgiveness in many directions: toward the self, toward others, and toward the past that lives in us. Too often, we treat forgiveness or reconciliation as a switch that makes everything better. For deeper wounds, it’s rarely that simple. Like grief, it can be a long, uneven process, with steps forward and steps back.

Through poetry, we will reflect on how forgiveness moves in public life and how this implicates us: who we decide is worthy of forgiveness, and what those decisions reveal about our values and allegiances. Poems about forgiving the one your love couldn’t reach, the one it overwhelmed, and forgiving yourself, again and again. Poems with awareness of how we fail, repair, and heal.
This session is facilitated by Featured Poet Furqan Mohamed Furqan Mohamed and Tender Possibilities’ founder, Farhia Tato

Furqan Mohamed is a writer, educator, and arts worker from Toronto interested in all things culture, kinship, and abolition. Her writing has appeared in Maisonneuve, FASHION, The Local, and C Mag. She is currently occupied by translation, and the ways hierarchies of knowledge sharing can be collapsed, from gallery spaces to the primary school classroom.

title: Pleasure with Sanna Wani
body:
Pleasure
as a means,
and then a
means again
with no ends
in sight.
– Eileen Myles

The upcoming session of Tender Possibilities explores the complexity of pleasure, held as a layered, shifting site and multidimensional practice. Together, we will trace how pleasure moves through language, how it resists containment, and how it can act as a politic, a pulse running through the everyday. We will consider how cultural invitations toward disembodiment shape us, and how poetry’s attention, curiosity, and intimacy can return us to the pleasures of language and of being.
This session will be facilitated by Featured Poet, Sanna Wani and Tender Possibilities’ founder, Farhia Tato.

Sanna Wani is the author of My Grief, the Sun (House of Anansi Press, 2022), the winner of the 2023 Trillium Award for Poetry. Her poetry and writing has been published by Brick, Hazlitt, Poem-A-Day among other places. She is a member of the Daybreak Poets Collective. She lives and writes in Toronto.

title: Devotion with wind in the leaves collective
image_alt: Devotion with wind in the leaves collective
body: 'Unless we can restore poetry to somewhere in the center of our universe, we are going to lose a lot of stars, a lot constellations, a lot of light.' — Kamau Brathwaite

For our upcoming session this month, we will explore devotion as attunement, as orientation, as return. A form of presence that moves through the spiritual, the political, and the intimate. Devotion shaped not only by longing and love, but by persistence and the willingness to remain in relation with what transforms us. To witness, and to offer something of ourselves in response.

Participants are invited to consider how devotion lives in the body and moves through the gestures of poetic language. Selected texts will guide our reflections as we weave poetry and movement, exploring how devotion can be expressed, felt, and reimagined through both ancestral and contemporary forms.
This session includes a performance by wind in the leaves collective, with artist director charles c. smith and Ranganathan Rajan.

wind in the leaves collective’s approach provides a unique view into a dialogue amongst artists on contemporary issues where the artists collaborate to create and share. The collective’s interdisciplinary approach allows for such engagement at several intersections, visceral, sensual, emotional, intellectual and spiritual. The themes the collective works on echo those of transnationalism, diaspora, globalization as well as the use/abuse of power and the
marginalization that results from it and wounds both individual and collective psyches.

charles c. smith is a poet, playwright and essayist who has written and edited twelve books and two chapbooks. He is currently working on his next book of poetry entitled Specimens which unearths the connections between western medical science and Black bodies. charles studied poetry and drama with William Packard at New York University and Herbert Berghof Studios, drama at the Frank Silvera’s Writers’ Workshop in Harlem.

Ranganathan Rajan (He/Him) is originally from India and is currently based in Tkaronto. He is a performer and choreographer in contemporary dance, working innately with ideas of stress, resilience, and strength in the body through object work, movement, and mixed media. Ranganathan graduated from the Professional Training Program at Dance Arts Institute Canada (2025) and has completed a Diploma in Movement Art and Mixed Media from Attakkalari Center of Movement Arts in Bangalore, India (2021).

title: Soul Rhythms with Lillian Allen
body: This session of Tender Possibilities moves through the political and spiritual frequencies of dub, spoken word, and sound poetry. Forms grounded in oral traditions that center the sonic textures of language. These poems emerge as a generative force in the ongoing (re)making of society, ideology, and aesthetics. Sung, spoken, chanted, and embodied as memory and medicine. Participants are invited to feel and inhabit these layered soundscapes, and to respond.
This session will be facilitated by Featured Poet Lillian Allen and Tender Possibilities’ founder, Farhia Tato.

Lillian Allen, Toronto's 7th Poet Laureate loves poetry like stars love the sky, like moonlight lights the night, and like how morning greets sunlight. Lillian Allen is an acclaimed foremother of Canadian poetry and has been working for decades exploring poetic languages of the soul, with word, before words, and beyond words. Lillian is also a leading international exponent, creator and innovator of dub poetry and spoken word, who travels internationally to read/perform her poetry. A mentor to the mentors, she has received numerous accolades and awards for her work and uplifting vision.

title: The Gaze with Tiana Reid
body: For the first session of Tender Possibilities' 2025 Summer Series, we’ll engage with curated poems to explore how surveillance, visibility, and power intersect to shape autonomy, self-expression, and identity. We invite participants to reflect on how both external and internalized forms of surveillance influence our lives, behaviours, and art.

Poetry is not a mirror held up to the world; it is a lens that reveals the profound implications of living in an era of constant observation. From drones and phone taps to algorithmic predictions and social media personas, our increasingly watched world challenges the notion of a private self. Poets, as keen observers, have long explored themes of privacy, identity, and truth. Poetry’s ability to contextualize technology and its social impact offers us tools for nuance, discernment, and resistance.
This session will be facilitated by Featured Poet Tiana Reid and Tender Possibilities’ founder, Farhia Tato.

Tiana Reid is an assistant professor in the English Department at York University, where she teaches black literature. Her writing has been published in Aperture, Momus, The Nation, The New York Review of Books, and elsewhere. She is working on a book of poetry called Nightnursing.
